passages.text: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K. This Item generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 are not included, and can be found in “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in Part II, Item 7 of the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 28, 2024. Product, Service and Software Announcements The Company announces new product, service and software offerings at various times during the year. Significant announcements during fiscal year 2025 included the following: First Quarter 2025: • MacBook Pro • Mac mini • iMac • iPad mini Second Quarter 2025: • iPhone 16e • iPad Air • iPad • MacBook Air • Mac Studio Third Quarter 2025: • iOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, iPadOS 26, watchOS 26, visionOS 26 and tvOS 26 Fourth Quarter 2025: • iPhone 17, iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max • Apple Watch Series 11, Apple Watch SE 3 and Apple Watch Ultra 3 • AirPods Pro 3 Fiscal Period The Company’s fiscal year is the 52- or 53-week period that ends on the last Saturday of September. An additional week is included in the first fiscal quarter every five or six years to realign the Company’s fiscal quarters with calendar quarters, which occurred in the first quarter of 2023. The Company’s fiscal years 2025 and 2024 spanned 52 weeks each, whereas fiscal year 2023 spanned 53 weeks. Macroeconomic Conditions Macroeconomic conditions, including inflation, interest rates and currency fluctuations, have directly and indirectly impacted, and could in the future materially impact, the Company’s results of operations and financial condition. Apple Inc. | 2025 Form 10-K | 21 Tariffs and Other Measures Beginning in the second quarter of 2025, new U.S. Tariffs were announced, including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the EU, among others. In response, several countries have imposed, or threatened to impose, reciprocal tariffs on imports from the U.S. and other retaliatory measures. Various modifications to the U.S. Tariffs have been announced and further changes could be made in the future, which may include additional sector-based tariffs or other measures. For example, the U.S. Department of Commerce has initiated an investigation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended, into, among other things, imports of semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, and their derivative products, including downstream products that contain semiconductors. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The following summarizes factors that could have a material adverse effect on the Company’s business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price. The Company may not be able to accurately predict, control or mitigate these risks. Statements in this section are based on the Company’s beliefs and opinions regarding matters that could materially adversely affect the Company in the future and are not representations as to whether such matters have or have not occurred previously. The risks and uncertainties described below are not exhaustive and should not be considered a complete statement of all potential risks or uncertainties that the Company faces or may face in the future. This section should be read in conjunction with Part II, Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes in Part II, Item 8, “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data” of this Form 10-K. Macroeconomic and Industry Risks The Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions and adverse economic conditions can materially adversely affect the Company’s business, results of operations, financial condition and stock price. The Company has international operations with sales outside the U.S. representing a majority of the Company’s total net sales. In addition, the Company’s global supply chain is large and complex and a majority of the Company’s supplier facilities, including manufacturing and assembly sites, are located outside the U.S. As a result, the Company’s operations and performance depend significantly on global and regional economic conditions. Adverse macroeconomic conditions, including slow growth or recession, high unemployment, inflation, tighter credit, higher interest rates, and currency fluctuations, can adversely impact consumer confidence and spending and materially adversely affect demand for the Company’s products and services. In addition, consumer confidence and spending can be materially adversely affected in response to changes in fiscal and monetary policy, financial market volatility, declines in income or asset values, and other economic factors. Uncertainty about, or a decline in, global or regional economic conditions can also have a significant impact on the Company’s suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics providers, distributors, cellular network carriers and other channel partners, and developers. Potential outcomes include financial instability; inability to obtain credit to finance business operations; and insolvency. Adverse economic conditions can also lead to increased credit and collectibility risk on the Company’s trade receivables; the failure of derivative counterparties and other financial institutions; limitations on the Company’s ability to issue new debt; reduced liquidity; and declines in the fair values of the Company’s financial instruments. credit_strengths.text: Apple's operating margin exceeds the sector median, reflecting premium pricing and a high-margin services mix. Operating income has grown steadily over the past three fiscal years, supporting strong internal cash generation. This profitability provides a substantial buffer against margin pressure from tariffs or component cost inflation, reinforcing the company's capacity to service debt from recurring earnings.

Operating cash flow covers debt by a wide margin, far above the sector median, and free cash flow approximates total debt. This cash conversion is a core credit strength, enabling Apple to fund dividends, buybacks, and maturities without relying on external financing. The consistency of cash generation across cycles supports a minimal indicative financial risk profile.

key_risks.text: The company faces material tariff and trade policy risk. New U.S. tariffs on imports from China, India, and other key manufacturing locations, plus potential reciprocal measures, could disrupt Apple's global supply chain, raise component costs, and pressure gross margins. The ultimate impact remains uncertain and depends on future policy changes, which could adversely affect results of operations and financial condition.

Apple's debt structure includes commercial paper and long-term borrowings, with a significant portion maturing beyond year five. While near-term maturities are manageable against cash flow, the company remains exposed to refinancing risk if credit markets tighten. Additionally, missing interest expense data prevents calculation of interest coverage, a material gap for assessing debt servicing capacity relative to sector peers.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow to debt is approximately one, indicating the company generates enough cash annually to repay total debt. This ratio is well above the sector median, underscoring strong debt servicing capacity. However, the absence of interest expense data limits a full assessment of coverage, though operating income alone provides a substantial cushion.

Net leverage, net of cash and short-term investments, is well below the sector median, reflecting a conservative capital structure. The company's cash balance and ongoing cash generation provide ample liquidity to meet maturities. Shareholder distributions absorb a large portion of free cash flow, but the remaining buffer still supports debt service without strain.

overall_credit_view.text: Apple's credit profile is exceptionally strong, with minimal leverage, robust cash flow, and a net cash position. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, and the company operates well within threshold headroom. While tariff and macroeconomic risks exist, the balance sheet and cash generation provide significant resilience. We view the credit as high quality with stable outlook.

The primary credit considerations are the company's exposure to global trade tensions and the lack of interest expense disclosure, which hinders precise coverage analysis. Nevertheless, operating income and cash flow are more than sufficient to service debt. We expect Apple to maintain its conservative financial policy, with shareholder returns funded from excess cash flow rather than incremental leverage.

credit_strengths.text: Apple的營業利潤率高於行業中位數，反映其溢價定價及高利潤率的服務組合。過去三個財政年度，營業收入穩步增長，支持強勁的內部現金生成。此盈利能力為關稅或組件成本通脹帶來的利潤率壓力提供了可觀的緩衝，鞏固了公司從經常性盈利中償還債務的能力。
營運現金流大幅覆蓋債務，遠高於行業中位數，而自由現金流接近總債務。此現金轉換是核心信用優勢，使Apple能夠在不依賴外部融資的情況下為股息、回購及到期債務提供資金。現金生成在各週期的一致性支持最低的指示性財務風險狀況。

key_risks.text: 公司面臨重大關稅及貿易政策風險。美國對來自中國、印度及其他主要製造地點的進口商品徵收新關稅，加上潛在的對等措施，可能擾亂Apple的全球供應鏈，提高組件成本，並對毛利率構成壓力。最終影響仍不確定，取決於未來政策變化，可能對經營業績及財務狀況造成不利影響。
Apple的債務結構包括商業票據及長期借款，其中相當部分在五年後到期。雖然近期到期債務相對現金流而言可控，但若信貸市場收緊，公司仍面臨再融資風險。此外，缺乏利息支出數據導致無法計算利息覆蓋率，這是評估相對於行業同行的債務償還能力的一個重大缺口。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流對債務比率約為一，表明公司每年產生的現金足以償還總債務。此比率遠高於行業中位數，突顯強勁的債務償還能力。然而，缺乏利息支出數據限制了對覆蓋率的全面評估，儘管僅營業收入已提供可觀的緩衝。
扣除現金及短期投資後的淨槓桿率遠低於行業中位數，反映保守的資本結構。公司的現金餘額及持續現金生成提供充足的流動性以滿足到期債務。股東分派佔用大部分自由現金流，但剩餘緩衝仍支持債務償還而無壓力。

overall_credit_view.text: Apple的信用狀況異常強勁，槓桿極低，現金流穩健，且處於淨現金狀態。指示性財務風險狀況為最低，公司營運遠在閾值餘量之內。儘管存在關稅及宏觀經濟風險，資產負債表及現金生成提供顯著韌性。我們認為該信用為高質量，展望穩定。
主要信用考量是公司對全球貿易緊張局勢的敞口，以及缺乏利息支出披露，這阻礙了精確的覆蓋率分析。儘管如此，營業收入及現金流足以償還債務。我們預期Apple將維持其保守的財務政策，股東回報由超額現金流而非增量槓桿提供資金。
